A_DATASET_DIMENSIONS.description: Synthetic patient queue dataset with 20,000 patient records and 26 features

C_TARGET_VARIABLE.name: waiting_time_minutes
C_TARGET_VARIABLE.description: Represents the actual waiting time in minutes for each patient - this is the primary prediction target
C_TARGET_VARIABLE.note: This is a clear, unambiguous target variable representing the expected waiting-time outcome

E_DUPLICATE_SUMMARY.note: No exact duplicate rows detected in the dataset

queue_and_position_features: patients_ahead (int) - Direct predictor of waiting time
queue_length_at_arrival (int) - Total queue load when patient arrived
token_number (int) - Sequential token assigned to patient
doctor_and_service_features: doctor_id (str categorical) - Doctor identity, affects service time
doctor_specialization (str categorical) - Medical specialty affects consultation duration
average_service_time_minutes (float) - Expected service duration per doctor
previous_patient_service_time (float) - Actual time for immediately prior patient
active_doctors (int) - Number of available doctors working
patient_and_visit_features: age (int) - Patient demographics, affects service complexity
patient_type (str) - New vs Follow-up affects consultation time
priority_level (str) - Urgent/Emergency patients affect queue dynamics
temporal_features: arrival_delay_minutes (float) - Time between scheduled and actual arrival
day_of_week (str categorical) - Operational patterns vary by day
operational_features: appointment_status (str) - Scheduled vs Walk-in affects queue flow

excluded_features.patient_id: Unique identifier; contains no predictive information, would cause overfitting
excluded_features.doctor_id: High-cardinality identifier; should use doctor_specialization as proxy or encode differently
excluded_features.visit_date: Temporal feature; convert to ordinal or use day_of_week instead
excluded_features.arrival_time: Temporal feature; requires parsing HH:MM format and conversion to meaningful features
excluded_features.scheduled_time: Temporal feature; same as arrival_time; calculate arrival_delay instead

previous_patient_service_time.reason: This is outcome information from a previous patient; it occurs AFTER the current patient joins queue but BEFORE prediction is made. Creates look-ahead bias.
previous_patient_service_time.recommendation: Use with caution or exclude from real-time prediction models; only safe for post-hoc analysis

average_service_time_minutes.reason: This appears to be historical average for each doctor. If recalculated on entire dataset, it may include future patient data.
average_service_time_minutes.recommendation: Use only if calculated from historical data strictly BEFORE prediction time

G_EXCLUDED_AND_LEAKY_FEATURES.note: Leakage detection is crucial for deployment; features must represent only information available at prediction time

numerical_features.recommendation: Standardize (Z-score) or normalize (0-1) to prevent large-scale features from dominating ML models
numerical_features.note: Important for distance-based and gradient descent algorithms

methods: One-Hot Encoding: gender, patient_type, appointment_status, day_of_week, doctor_specialization
categorical_features.note: Categorical features must be converted to numerical representations for ML models

arrival_delay_minutes.recommendation: Impute with 0 (assumed on-time arrival) or median; or use as indicator variable

previous_patient_service_time.recommendation: Impute with average_service_time_minutes or use forward-fill within doctor groups

staff_availability.recommendation: Impute with median or use business hours average

time_feature_engineering.recommendation: Extract hour from arrival_time and scheduled_time; create is_rush_hour, is_morning, etc.
time_feature_engineering.note: Temporal patterns likely affect queue dynamics significantly

target_distribution.observation: waiting_time_minutes ranges from 1 to 240 minutes with median of 66 minutes
target_distribution.implication: Distribution is likely right-skewed; consider log transformation or quantile-based evaluation metrics

missing_data_pattern.implication: This feature may be meaningful only for subset of data; consider stratified analysis

feature_uniqueness.observation: patient_id has 20,000 unique values; doctor_id has ~27 unique values; day_of_week has 7 unique values
feature_uniqueness.implication: Patient ID should never be used; doctor specialization is better predictor than doctor ID

categorical_balance.observation: Gender: Female/Male/Other; Priority: Normal/Urgent/Emergency; Patient Type: New/Follow-up
categorical_balance.implication: Check class imbalance; Emergency patients likely have different queue dynamics

correlation_potential.observation: patients_ahead, queue_length, and doctor availability likely correlate strongly with waiting time
correlation_potential.implication: These are the PRIMARY PREDICTORS; multicollinearity may be an issue

synthetic_data_note.observation: This is a synthetic dataset created for academic purposes
synthetic_data_note.implication: Results should not be claimed as clinically validated; patterns may differ from real data

J_RECOMMENDATIONS_FOR_NEXT_ML_STEP: 1. EXPLORATORY DATA ANALYSIS (EDA) CONTINUATION
- Create scatter plots of target vs key numeric features (patients_ahead, queue_length, service_time)
- Analyze distribution of waiting_time_minutes by priority_level, day_of_week, doctor_specialization
- Compute correlation matrix for numeric features to detect multicollinearity
- Examine temporal patterns: peak_hour effect, day_of_week patterns
2. DATA CLEANING AND PREPROCESSING
- Handle missing values: arrival_delay_minutes, previous_patient_service_time, staff_availability
- Remove or encode patient_id, visit_date, arrival_time, scheduled_time
- Create meaningful time features (hour, is_peak, is_weekend, etc.)
- Encode categorical variables appropriately
3. TRAIN-TEST SPLIT STRATEGY
- Use temporal split if data has time ordering (RECOMMENDED for time-series queue data)
- Or use stratified random split by priority_level to maintain distribution
- Reserve test set for final model evaluation ONLY
4. FEATURE ENGINEERING
- Interaction features: patients_ahead * average_service_time, queue_length * active_doctors
- Ratio features: queue_length / active_doctors (queue intensity)
- Temporal features: is_morning, is_afternoon, is_rush_hour from arrival_time/scheduled_time
5. MODEL SELECTION
- BASELINE: Linear Regression (simple, interpretable, fast)
- TREE-BASED: Decision Trees, Random Forests, XGBoost (handle non-linearity and feature importance)
- GRADIENT BOOSTING: LightGBM (fast, memory-efficient for production)
- Start with tree-based models; they typically excel at queue prediction problems
- Use cross-validation (k-fold) for robust evaluation
6. MODEL EVALUATION METRICS
- Primary: Mean Absolute Error (MAE) in minutes (interpretable for waiting time)
- Secondary: Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) (penalizes large errors more)
- Tertiary: R² Score (proportion of variance explained)
- Also report: Median Absolute Error, 95th percentile error (worst-case waiting time)
7. HANDLE LEAKAGE BEFORE TRAINING
- EXCLUDE or handle carefully: previous_patient_service_time
- VERIFY: average_service_time_minutes is computed from historical data only
- Simulate real-time prediction scenario: only use information available BEFORE patient joins queue
8. HYPERPARAMETER TUNING
- Use GridSearchCV or RandomizedSearchCV with cross-validation
- Tune tree depth, learning rate, number of estimators (for ensemble models)
- Monitor for overfitting: compare train vs validation metrics
9. FEATURE IMPORTANCE ANALYSIS
- After training: rank features by importance for interpretability
- Expected top features: patients_ahead, queue_length, average_service_time, active_doctors
- Use SHAP values for detailed feature impact analysis
10. MODEL DEPLOYMENT PREPARATION
- Save trained model using joblib (approved for project use)
- Document: feature engineering pipeline, preprocessing steps, expected input format
- Create prediction function that accepts queue context (patients_ahead, queue_length, etc.)
- Prepare for Flask/FastAPI integration with Node.js backend
11. VALIDATION AND TESTING
- Test on held-out test set
- Simulate real-time prediction: feed features in same format as production
- Check edge cases: empty queue, peak hour, multiple doctors
12. DOCUMENTATION
- Document all preprocessing steps for reproducibility
- Note: synthetic dataset, no clinical validation claimed
- Record model performance metrics for final report
